extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders who wish to comment on or intervene in FERC Docket No. CP21-94-004 (e.g., landowners, municipalities, organizations, ratepayers, environmental justice and Tribal communities, businesses)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural requirements for filing comments, protests, and motions to intervene in a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission proceeding (Docket No. CP21-94-004), including methods of submission, content expectations, deadlines, service rules, and rights of intervenors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person wishing to comment on the request may do so. Comments may include statements of support or objections, to the request as a whole or specific aspects of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The more specific your comments, the more useful they will be. Comments do not make the filer a party to the proceeding; to become a party, you must intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to submit comments
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three methods to submit comments or protests: (1) eComment (brief, text-only), (2) eFiling (attach files), and (3) paper mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing electronically reference the docket number. eComment is located on FERC's site under Documents and Filings. eFiling allows attachments; new eFiling users must create an account via eRegister and select filing type (General -> Comment on a Filing). Paper filings must reference the docket number and be mailed to the Acting Secretary at the addresses provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to reference docket number
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must reference the docket number CP21-94-004 in the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to comments, protests, and motions to intervene so the filing is timely and properly recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest eligibility and content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file a protest to the application pursuant to sections 157.10(a)(4) and 385.211 of the Commission's regulations under the NGA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests must comply with the requirements specified in section 385.2001 of the Commission's regulations. A protest may also serve as a motion to intervene if the protestor states it also seeks intervenor status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness for comments and protests
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure that your comments or protests are timely and properly recorded, submit them on or before October 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submissions may not be considered; follow the stated deadline (5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 1, 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may intervene
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person (including individuals, organizations, businesses, municipalities, and other entities) has the option to file a motion to intervene in this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not need to have property directly impacted to intervene. For individuals, state known positions and interests (e.g., landowner, ratepayer, resident of an impacted community, or recreationist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to intervene content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to intervene must state, to the extent known, your position regarding the proceeding and your interest in the proceeding as required by Rule 214.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe your stake (status as landowner, ratepayer, resident, recreationist, etc.). Failure to state position/interest may affect intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to file a motion to intervene
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to intervene can be filed (1) via eFiling or (2) by paper copy (with three copies) mailed to the Acting Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For eFiling, new users must eRegister and select 'General' then 'Intervention'. The eFiling feature includes a document-less intervention option (see provided link). Paper motions must reference docket number CP21-94-004.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic grant of timely, unopposed interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: All timely, unopposed motions to intervene are automatically granted by operation of Rule 214(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If intervention is unopposed and timely, no further action is required for party status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late interventions and good cause requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to intervene filed after the intervention deadline are untimely and may be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A late-filed motion must show good cause for being late, explain why the time limitation should be waived, and provide justification by reference to factors set forth in Rule 214(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and consequences of intervenor status
rubrics_metrics.description: Only intervenors have the right to request rehearing of Commission orders issued in this proceeding and to subsequently challenge the Commission's orders in the U.S. Circuit Courts of Appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An intervenor will be placed on the service list and receive copies (paper or electronic) of all documents filed by the applicant and all other parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements for protests and interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests and motions to intervene must be served on the applicant at the provided mailing or email address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent submissions by an intervenor must be served on the applicant and all other parties. Service can be via email with a link to the document. Party contact information can be downloaded from the service list at the eService link on FERC Online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing is free
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fee or cost for filing comments or intervening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explicitly states there is no fee or cost for filing comments or intervening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eComment for brief text-only submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: eComment is an easy method for interested persons to submit brief, text-only comments on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use eComment for short comments rather than uploading documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eFiling for attachments and fuller submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: eFiling allows you to provide comments in a variety of formats by attaching them as a file with your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New eFiling users must eRegister. When filing select the type 'General' then appropriate subtype ('Comment on a Filing' or 'Intervention').

rubrics_metrics.name: Document availability and official source verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The full text of the application and this document are available on FERC's eLibrary in PDF and Microsoft Word format; the Federal Register PDF on govinfo.gov is the official electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User assistance is available for eLibrary and the Commission's website. Verify results against the official edition for legal research; the XML FederalRegister.gov is informational and not legal notice until ACFR grants official status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance resources for public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's Office of Public Participation (OPP) and FERC Online Support can assist members of the public with accessing information and making filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact OPP at (202) 502-6595 or OPP@ferc.gov for assistance including landowners, EJ communities, Tribal members. eFiling staff available at (202) 502-8258 or FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov. Public Reference Room contacts are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking the proceeding via eSubscription and eLibrary
rubrics_metrics.description: Use eLibrary to access formal documents and eSubscription to keep track of issuances and submittals in specific dockets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eSubscription provides notification of filings, document summaries, and direct links to documents, reducing research time. Register at the provided FERC link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service list and document service format
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons obtaining party status will be placed on the service list maintained by the Secretary and will receive copies (paper or electronic) of all documents filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service can be electronic; contact information for parties can be downloaded from eService.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest may also serve as motion to intervene
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest may serve as a motion to intervene so long as the protestor states it also seeks to be an intervenor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the protest includes an explicit statement seeking intervenor status and satisfies intervention content requirements.
